cases.description: When the zone does not contain any RRsets for the supplied name, `exactName(name)` returns null, causing `findExactMatch` to return null regardless of the requested type.

group: findExactMatch - exact type match (oneRRset returns RRset)

cases.expected: RRset instance containing the A record for www.example.
cases.description: The zone contains an A record for `www.example.`. `exactName(name)` returns a non‑null object, and `oneRRset(types, type)` finds the RRset matching the requested type, so the method returns that RRset.

group: findExactMatch - name present but type absent (oneRRset returns null)

cases.description: The zone contains records for `mail.example.` (e.g., MX), but no SRV records. `exactName(name)` returns a non‑null object, however `oneRRset(types, type)` cannot find an RRset for the SRV type and returns null, which `findExactMatch` propagates.
Passing a null `Name` should cause `exactName(name)` to throw a NullPointerException (or the method to fail early). The test verifies that the exception is thrown.

group: findExactMatch - origin name with SOA type

cases.expected: RRset instance containing the SOA record for the zone apex (example.)
cases.description: The zone apex (origin) always has an SOA RRset. When `findExactMatch` is called with the origin name and type SOA, `exactName` returns a non‑null object and `oneRRset` finds the SOA RRset, which should be returned.

group: findExactMatch - origin name with NS type

cases.expected: RRset instance containing the NS records for the zone apex (example.)
cases.description: The zone apex also contains NS records. The method should return the NS RRset when queried with the origin name and type NS.

group: findExactMatch - name with multiple RRsets, each type retrieved correctly

cases.expected: RRset instance containing the A record(s) for www.example.
cases.description: The name `www.example.` has both A and AAAA records. Requesting type A must return the A RRset.

cases.expected: RRset instance containing the AAAA record(s) for www.example.
cases.description: The same name queried for AAAA must return the AAAA RRset, proving that `findExactMatch` can distinguish between multiple RRsets belonging to the same name.
`Type.ANY` (value 0) is not a concrete RR type. `oneRRset` cannot match it, so `findExactMatch` should return null even though the name exists in the zone.

group: findExactMatch - request invalid negative type returns null

cases.description: A negative type value is not a valid DNS RR type. The implementation should treat it as not found and return null rather than throwing.

group: findExactMatch - name with CNAME, request CNAME type returns RRset

cases.expected: RRset instance containing the CNAME record for alias.example.
cases.description: The name `alias.example.` is defined as a CNAME. When queried for type CNAME the method must return the corresponding RRset.

group: findExactMatch - name with CNAME, request A type returns null

cases.description: Even though `alias.example.` exists, it only has a CNAME record. Requesting type A should yield null because `oneRRset` cannot find an A RRset for that name.

group: findExactMatch - empty zone returns null for any name

cases.description: When the `Zone` instance contains no records at all, `exactName` will always return null, causing `findExactMatch` to return null for any name/type combination.

group: findExactMatch - name with DNSSEC RRSIG type returns RRset

cases.expected: RRset instance containing the RRSIG records for www.example.
cases.description: If DNSSEC signatures are present for `www.example.`, a request for type RRSIG should retrieve the corresponding RRset.

group: findExactMatch - type value exceeds DNS maximum (65535)

cases.description: The DNS type field is limited to 16 bits (0‑65535). Supplying a value larger than the maximum should cause the internal `oneRRset` validation to throw an IllegalArgumentException, which propagates out of `findExactMatch`.
Using an extreme integer for the type argument should be rejected by the method (or by `oneRRset`) as it is not a valid DNS RR type, resulting in an IllegalArgumentException.
The `Name` class requires an absolute (fully‑qualified) name for zone look‑ups. Passing a relative name should cause `exactName` (or an earlier validation step) to throw an IllegalArgumentException.

group: findExactMatch - internal state corruption triggers IllegalStateException

cases.description: If the zone's internal data structures are corrupted (e.g., the map used by `exactName` is null), the private method may throw IllegalStateException. The test forces this condition (by mocking or reflection) and verifies that the exception propagates.
